title: Inherited peculiarities appear in offspring at the age they appeared in parent

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Inherited peculiarities appear in offspring at the age they appeared in parent

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: A peculiarity tends to appear in the offspring at the same period of life at which it first appeared in the parent, though sometimes earlier.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: A much more important rule, which I think may be trusted, is that, at whatever period of life a peculiarity first appears, it tends to appear in the offspring at a corresponding age, though sometimes earlier.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter I, “Variation under Domestication”; section “Inheritance”. Scope: domesticated animals and plants, extended to organisms generally

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch01-06: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.56

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The statistic is straightforward, but datasets linking pedigrees to repeated age-specific traits are scattered and biased toward disease. Only limited domains can be tested now.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In pedigrees with longitudinal phenotyping, compare age of onset of a heritable trait in parents and offspring against shuffled parent-offspring pairs. Positive age concordance supports the rule; no concordance refutes it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Age of first parental appearance is rarely recorded.

Disease onset is an imperfect proxy for any peculiarity.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.29
discriminating power: 0.65
operationalizability: 0.79
analysis feasibility: 0.56
data existence: 0.54

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Age-of-onset correlation is a clear statistic, and an animal Mendelian catalogue contains pieces of it for domestic species. It is not a parent-offspring age table, and plants are barely represented, so coverage is a thin subset of the stated scope. Developmental necessity and shared environment keep a positive correlation from uniquely supporting a special inheritance-timing rule.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Regress offspring age at first expression of a peculiarity on parental age at first expression, allowing an earlier-offspring class, for inherited diseases and life-stage traits. A positive age match, with a minority of earlier offspring onsets, would support the rule; ages of onset scattered independently of the parent's age would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
OMIA rarely pairs a specific parent's onset age with the offspring's onset age.

Shared rearing environment can align ages of onset without an inheritance rule about timing.

Many characters can be expressed at only one developmental stage, so a matching age is obligatory.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.66
discriminating power: 0.48
analysis feasibility: 0.42
data existence: 0.45
data adequacy: 0.32
